introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0585 RELIGIOUS STUDIES 1, JUNE 2018, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so; check that the booklet is headed Ordinary Level - 0585 Religious Studies 1. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. All questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question; if you change your mind, erase the first mark carefully, then mark your new answer. Avoid spending too much time on any one question. Do all your rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces. At the end of the examination the invigilator collects the answer sheet first and then the question booklet. Printed heading of the question pages: Personal and Social Relationships and Problems, answer all 50 questions.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following can enhance true friendship?

*Options as printed:* A) Sympathy   B) Riches   C) Empathy   D) Honesty
questions.corrige_markdown:
True friendship is built on trust, and trust rests on honesty. Riches do not build friendship. Sympathy and empathy also help, which is why the printed question is not clear-cut; the usual textbook answer is honesty.

**Intended answer: D (Honesty).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - friendship and love

questions.enonce_markdown: Friendship can come to an end when one person
questions.corrige_markdown: A friendship is a two-way relationship of giving and receiving. A person who thinks only of himself or herself stops giving, and the friendship breaks down. Depending on someone, being richer or loving more do not in themselves end a friendship. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - friendship and love

questions.enonce_markdown:
One important reason why fornication must be avoided is because it

*Options as printed:* A) can lead to pregnancy.   B) can lead to HIV/AIDS.   C) is against God's commandment.   D) breaks marriages.
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to Christian teaching, sexual intercourse belongs within marriage, so fornication is against God's commandment. Pregnancy and disease are possible consequences, but the moral reason given by the programme is the divine law. Several options are defensible, so the printed question is not reliable for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: C (is against God's commandment).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown: The highest love is manifested in
questions.corrige_markdown: According to Christian teaching, the greatest commandment is to love God above everything, and love of neighbor flows from it. The other forms of love come after it. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - friendship and love

questions.enonce_markdown: Sexual abuse of a child by an adult is
questions.corrige_markdown: Paedophilia is the sexual abuse of, or attraction to, children by adults. Abduction is carrying someone away by force, and masochism is taking pleasure in one's own pain. Rape is forced sex in general, not specifically the abuse of a child. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown: A marriage in which a man has more than one wife or a woman has more than one husband is called
questions.corrige_markdown: Polygamy is the general word for marriage with more than one spouse. Polygyny is only one man with several wives, polyandry only one woman with several husbands, and bigamy is having exactly two spouses. Only polygamy covers both cases in the question. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: An official statement putting an end to civil marriage is called
questions.corrige_markdown: Divorce is the legal act by which a court ends a valid civil marriage. An annulment declares that the marriage never validly existed, and separation does not end the marriage bond. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: Commutative justice is also called
questions.corrige_markdown: Commutative justice governs fair exchange between individuals, such as honoring contracts and paying agreed prices, so it is also called contractual justice. Distributive justice concerns what society owes its members, and contributive (social) justice what members owe society. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: Peace is not only the absence of war but also the presence of
questions.corrige_markdown: Lasting peace requires fair treatment of people, so peace is understood as the fruit of justice. Without justice, quarrels and violence return even when there is no open war. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: This type of love is intense, full of excitement and does not last long.
questions.corrige_markdown: Infatuation is a strong but shallow attraction that fades quickly. Agape is selfless, lasting love, conjugal love is the love between spouses, and filial love is the love between parent and child. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - friendship and love

questions.enonce_markdown: Embezzlement leads to capital flight because
questions.corrige_markdown: Embezzled public money is often sent abroad and kept in foreign banks, so it leaves the country's economy. That outflow of capital is what is called capital flight. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - corruption and embezzlement

questions.enonce_markdown: An attempt to foretell the future by use of lifeless objects is called
questions.corrige_markdown: Divination is the attempt to learn about the future or hidden things by reading objects or signs, such as cowries or cards. Sorcery and witchcraft are the use of supposed powers to harm, and superstition is an unfounded belief. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sects and cults

questions.enonce_markdown:
Artificial birth control is the use of

*Options as printed:* A) chemical and mechanical means to prevent pregnancy.   B) condoms during sexual intercourse.   C) man-made methods to prevent pregnancy.   D) pills to avoid pregnancy.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Artificial birth control means preventing pregnancy by chemical (pills, injections) and mechanical (condoms, devices) means, as opposed to natural methods. Condoms and pills are only examples. Option C is also a defensible wording, so the printed question is not reliable for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: A (chemical and mechanical means to prevent pregnancy).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: Civil liberty is the right of citizens to
questions.corrige_markdown: Civil liberties are the basic freedoms guaranteed to citizens, such as freedom of expression, political freedom and freedom of association. They are limited by law and by the rights of others, so not 'whatever they want'. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - civil liberties

questions.enonce_markdown: The transfer of public funds to private accounts is called
questions.corrige_markdown: Embezzlement is the dishonest taking of funds entrusted to one's care, especially public money, for personal use. Capital flight is the movement of money out of a country, which is a consequence of it. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - corruption and embezzlement

questions.enonce_markdown:
Sects and Cults are similar in the following ways EXCEPT that

*Options as printed:* A) their leaders do not manipulate them.   B) both do not deal with secrecy.   C) both are everywhere.   D) sects are religious while cults are demonic.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The printed question is defective: options A and B both state something false about sects and cults (both are usually led by manipulating leaders and both are secretive), and D states a difference rather than a similarity. The intended answer is most likely A, but the question is left open.

**Intended answer: A (their leaders do not manipulate them).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sects and cults

questions.enonce_markdown: What is a family which is made up of father, mother and children?
questions.corrige_markdown: A nuclear family consists of the parents and their children only. An extended family includes other relatives such as grandparents, uncles and aunts. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown:
One who owns a house in some other region but resides in another is

*Options as printed:* A) Vagus.   B) Incola.   C) Advena.   D) Peregrinus.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Latin terms come from the vocabulary of residence in Church law: a vagus has no fixed home, a peregrinus is outside his place of residence, an incola is one who lives in a place, and an advena is a newcomer or temporary resident. The printed question depends on a local textbook convention, so it is not reliable for automatic marking. The most likely intended answer is advena.

**Intended answer: C (Advena).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown:
Natural family planning is normally accepted because it

*Options as printed:* A) helps to space out children.   B) is a reliable method of birth control.   C) does not interfere with the natural process of life.   D) respects the bodies of the spouses.
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to Catholic and many Christian teachings, natural family planning uses the woman's natural cycle and does not interfere with the natural process of life, unlike artificial methods. Spacing children is its purpose, not the reason it is accepted. Other options are defensible, so the question is left open.

**Intended answer: C (does not interfere with the natural process of life).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: Surrogacy is
questions.corrige_markdown: In surrogacy a woman carries a pregnancy for another person or couple, which is why it is called womb hiring or womb renting. Egg donation and embryo transfer are other fertility techniques. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a moral argument against the use of condoms?
questions.corrige_markdown: According to Christian moral teaching, the objection to condoms is moral: they are said to encourage sex outside marriage and so promote promiscuity. Reduced pleasure, effectiveness and cost are practical, not moral, arguments. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown: What does the HIV attack in the human body?
questions.corrige_markdown: HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) attacks the immune system, destroying the white blood cells that fight infection, which leads to AIDS. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - hiv and aids

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following can best guarantee justice in a society?

*Options as printed:* A) The laws.   B) The lawyers.   C) The magistrates.   D) The fear of God.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Laws, applied equally to all, set the standard for fair treatment. Lawyers and magistrates only apply them. The printed question is a matter of opinion (the fear of God is also defensible), so it is left open; the likely intended answer is the laws.

**Intended answer: A (The laws).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown:
One basic reason why people ought to work is that

*Options as printed:* A) they work to eat.   B) they are forced to work.   C) all human beings must work.   D) idleness is evil.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The basic reason for work is to earn a living and meet needs such as food. Other options are defensible according to different texts, and the printed question is not clear, so it is left open; the likely intended answer is that people work to eat.

**Intended answer: A (they work to eat).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - work and unemployment

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is the first consequence of justice?
questions.corrige_markdown: Peace is described as the first fruit of justice: where people are treated fairly, conflict is reduced and progress and development can follow. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: When a drug is taken for a reason other than health, it is known as
questions.corrige_markdown: Drug abuse is the use of a drug for a purpose other than medical treatment. Addiction is dependence on the drug, and misuse is wrong use of a medicine (wrong dose, for instance). **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - drugs and substance abuse

questions.enonce_markdown:
Human life is precious because it is

*Options as printed:* A) a gift from God.   B) an inalienable right.   C) made in God's image.   D) an alienable right.
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to Christian teaching, human beings are created in the image of God, which gives life its special value. Option A is also defensible, and the printed question is therefore left open.

**Intended answer: C (made in God's image).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: The termination of a pregnancy because it endangers the life of the mother is
questions.corrige_markdown: Therapeutic abortion is the termination of a pregnancy for medical reasons, in particular to save the mother's life. A miscarriage is spontaneous, and induced abortion is a general term. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: The best conscience to follow is the ____ conscience.
questions.corrige_markdown: A certain conscience is sure that an act is right or wrong and can be followed. Scrupulous, perplexed and doubtful consciences are uncertain and cannot be relied on. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - conscience and moral choice

questions.enonce_markdown: Sexual intercourse between close family members is called
questions.corrige_markdown: Incest is sexual relations between close relatives. Fornication is between unmarried people, adultery involves a married person, and rape is forced intercourse. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown: We should respect our bodies because we
questions.corrige_markdown: According to Christian teaching, the body is created by God and is to be respected as a gift, so respect for it is a religious duty and not only a legal or health matter. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the following is NOT a consequence of a badly formed conscience:
questions.corrige_markdown: A badly formed conscience leads to wrong decisions without guilt, going against God's will and being prone to evil. Moral rigour (strict uprightness) is a sign of a well-formed conscience. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - conscience and moral choice

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is NOT a form of marriage?

*Options as printed:* A) Customary marriage.   B) Civil status marriage.   C) Traditional marriage.   D) Traditional court marriage.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Marriage is usually described as customary or traditional, civil (before the civil authority) and religious. The wording of options B and D is not standard, so the printed question is defective and left open. The likely intended answer is B.

**Intended answer: B (Civil status marriage).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: Someone who is hired and is paid for a job is called
questions.corrige_markdown: An employee is hired by an employer and paid for the work done. The employer is the one who hires. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - work and unemployment

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these methods is used by sects to attract new members?
questions.corrige_markdown: Sects often attract followers by promising healing and miracles. Practicing what they preach does not describe the manipulative methods of sects, and carrying a Bible or playing music is not specific to them. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sects and cults

questions.enonce_markdown: Fraud is
questions.corrige_markdown: Fraud is deceiving others by tricks in order to obtain money or advantage. Stealing is simply taking something, and telling lies is only one means. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - corruption and embezzlement

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following features is common among members of a sect?

*Options as printed:* A) Unity among members.   B) Common interest of all.   C) Quoting the scriptures.   D) Commitment to the leaders.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Members of a sect show strong commitment and obedience to their leaders. The other options are defensible features of many groups, so the printed question is not reliable for automatic marking and is left open.

**Intended answer: D (Commitment to the leaders).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sects and cults

questions.enonce_markdown: A person who has no home and wanders about is called
questions.corrige_markdown: A vagus is a person with no fixed home who wanders about. A traveler has a home, a peregrinus is a foreigner or visitor away from home, and an incola is a settled resident. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: The main purpose of Trade Unions is
questions.corrige_markdown: Trade unions defend workers' interests, above all by improving working conditions and pay. Output and quality are concerns of management, and preventing dismissal is only one part of their work. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - work and unemployment

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following factors can encourage people to work hard?

*Options as printed:* A) Working hours.   B) Working environment.   C) Salary.   D) Promotions at work.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Several factors motivate workers, and the printed question does not say which is meant, so it is left open. The likely intended answer is salary, since pay is the first motive for working.

questions.enonce_markdown: The use of violent acts to frighten citizens as a way of trying to achieve a political goal is
questions.corrige_markdown: Terrorism is the use of violence and fear against civilians to obtain a political aim. War is armed conflict between groups, mutiny is revolt by soldiers, and secession is breaking away from a state. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Leisure is an activity carried out
questions.corrige_markdown: Leisure is free time used for rest and recreation, which relieves stress and restores energy. It is not meant to avoid work or reduce it. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Someone who has given up the right to marry in order to serve God is a
questions.corrige_markdown: A celibate is a person who chooses not to marry, in order to serve God. A bachelor or spinster is simply unmarried, without a religious reason. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of these is a primary cause of global warming?

*Options as printed:* A) Depletion of the Ozone layer.   B) Direct rays of the sun.   C) Release of carbon monoxide.   D) Burning of bushes.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Global warming is caused mainly by greenhouse gases, above all carbon dioxide, produced by burning fuels and vegetation. None of the printed options names carbon dioxide, so the question is defective and left open. The likely intended answer is the release of carbon gases.

**Intended answer: C (Release of carbon monoxide).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - environmental ethics

questions.enonce_markdown: When one parent is forced by circumstances to bring up children alone, he or she is a
questions.corrige_markdown: A single parent raises children alone, whether the cause is death, separation or other circumstances. 'Single mother' and 'widow' cover only part of the cases. **Answer: C.**
